clue.text: A university man unknown on the river

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a university graduate
Z is an algebraic unknown
taken as written

explanation.surface: A graduate of unknown name is out boating.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amazon is the great South American waterway.

clue.text: Battle, possibly, for such high ecclesiastical office

definitions.text: Battle, possibly, for such high ecclesiastical office

parts.words: Battle, possibly, for such high ecclesiastical office
parts.note: Battle in Sussex has a famous abbey, whose head would hold this senior church post; the comma hides the town behind a fight

explanation.surface: Someone may fight for a top church post.
explanation.walkthrough: Battle is a town in Sussex, England, named after the 1066 battle and home to Battle Abbey; an abbot's office goes with such a place.
explanation.definitionFit: The office or tenure of an abbot is a senior church position.

clue.text: Estranged woman sheltered by girl and boy

indicators.note: a thing sheltered by others sits between them, so one name goes inside the other two

parts.note: Ali is a girl's name, short for Alison
Ted is a boy's name
Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman cut off from family is taken in by a young couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone alienated has been made unfriendly or cut off, as an estranged relative is.

clue.text: Mostly comply with directions associated with large corporation

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word for comply loses its final letter

parts.note: to obey is to comply
S and E are compass directions, south and east

explanation.surface: Following instructions as dictated by a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is old slang for a big belly, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A large paunch, jocularly a corporation, goes with being very fat.

clue.text: Female long on cheek might well be this

definitions.text: Female long on cheek might well be this

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the yearning comes after the insolence

parts.note: lip means cheek, insolence
to pant for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: A woman who loves backchat would naturally be like this.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who longs to give cheek would be glib and irreverent.

clue.text: Shrub's flower cut across

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the bloom loses its last letter

parts.note: a lily is a flower
AC is the usual abbreviation for across

explanation.surface: A gardener slices through a bush's bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The lilac is a flowering bush with fragrant purple or white blossom.

clue.text: E.g. McGonagall dipping into The Raven?

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote the poem The Raven, so the poem stands for its author
one who is dipping into food or a book is a taster

explanation.surface: A Scottish versifier browses a famous American poem.
explanation.walkthrough: William McGonagall was a Victorian Scottish poet famous as the worst in the language; here the poem is its author and the dipper a sampler.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of trashy verse is a bad poet, and McGonagall is the classic instance.

clue.text: Greek screen with ends trimmed

indicators.note: trimming both ends removes the first and last letters of the word for screen

parts.note: a lattice is a screen of crossed strips

explanation.surface: A Greek screen is cut down at both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Attic means of Attica or Athens, so Athenian or Greek.

clue.text: Vigorous description of an American boneshaker?

definitions.meaning: an old bicycle without rubber tyres, spelt the American way, would be without them

explanation.surface: An energetic old American bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: A boneshaker is an early bicycle with solid wheels; Americans spell tyre TIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unflagging never runs out of energy, which is vigour.

clue.text: Characters assumed to take exercise, with strange reason

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: strange tells us the letters of reason appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Actors adopt roles to justify a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Personae are roles or masks that a writer or actor takes on.

clue.text: Display good horsemanship escorting leader of brigands into jail

indicators.note: an escort walks beside, so the riding phrase goes alongside, after the bandit's initial
the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to ride well is to show skill on horseback

explanation.surface: A rider shows off while taking a bandit chief to prison.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London prison, and the name became a general word for a jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, a former London house of correction, became a generic name for a prison.

clue.text: Always carrying books to make records

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: e'er is a poetic form of ever, always
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone forever lugging books around to keep logs.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter details is to write them down in a ledger or register.

clue.text: Reportedly masters something that's child's play

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: conquers means masters, overcomes

explanation.surface: Rumour says that someone has mastered a simple task.
explanation.walkthrough: Conkers is a British schoolchildren's game played with horse chestnuts on strings.
explanation.definitionFit: This chestnut-smashing game is literally played by children.

clue.text: Part of church where Liberal appears fortuitously?

parts.note: fortuitously means by chance
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: A churchgoer of the Liberal party turns up in the sanctuary by luck.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the area round the altar, used by clergy and choir.

clue.text: Become active and move own cricket gear

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning get moving, bestir yourself
literally, to shift one's wickets, the stumps used in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer gets going and shifts the wickets.
explanation.walkthrough: Stumps are the three upright sticks of a cricket wicket.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to start moving quickly, to get going.

clue.text: Deciphered a grim character's rambling tale

indicators.note: deciphered means worked out from a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a role is a character played on stage

explanation.surface: A gloomy figure's long story has been decoded.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigmarole is a long, confused, wandering story or procedure.

clue.text: Woman Sir Patrick kept in a state of uncertainty

indicators.note: one name is kept inside the other, so the knight sits within the woman's name

parts.note: Sue is a woman's name
Sir Patrick Spens is the hero of a famous Scottish ballad

explanation.surface: A woman keeps a knight dangling, unsure of his fate.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is anxious uncertainty about what will happen.

clue.text: Milky wash splashed around in drippy fashion

indicators.note: something splashed around is thrown about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Milky water slops everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Mawkish means sickly sentimental, which is what drippy suggests.

clue.text: Just so books ought to be

definitions.meaning: accounts should have debits and credits equal

explanation.surface: Accounts should be fair and correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A balanced view is fair, and balanced books have debits equal to credits.

clue.text: In response to reference marks, stressed and up in arms

definitions.meaning: daggers are printers' reference marks, so these would be drawn when called for
openly hostile and ready to fight

explanation.surface: Tense and angry in reply to footnote symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: The dagger sign marks a footnote in print, so 'reference marks' stands for daggers.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes two parties in bitter hostility, as if blades were out.

clue.text: Sinew displayed by heavyweight securing goal

indicators.note: securing means holding fast inside, so the aim is put within the weight

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A big boxer shows muscle while scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon is a tough cord joining muscle to bone, a sinew.

clue.text: Pitch where snake appears to proceed hesitatingly

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
to halt is to walk with a limp or waver

explanation.surface: A serpent slithers haltingly across the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is a tarry substance, and asphalt is a bitumen surfacing mixture.

clue.text: Creature with father's letters

parts.note: the letters of pa, a word for father, are P and A
and means with, together
the letters of pa, a word for father, are P and A

explanation.surface: An animal comes with a letter from Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as P and A, the two letters of PA.
explanation.definitionFit: The panda is a bear-like animal from China.

clue.text: Conservative involved in genuine ceasefire

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: true means genuine

explanation.surface: A Tory takes part in a real cessation of hostilities.
explanation.definitionFit: A truce is an agreed halt to fighting.

clue.text: Hard rubber in erasers originally to be recycled

indicators.note: recycled means remade, so the pooled letters are rearranged
originally points to the opening letter of the word erasers

explanation.surface: Rubbers in pencil erasers will be reused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recycled' rearranges IN, E (from 'erasers originally') and TO BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebonite is vulcanite, a hard black vulcanised rubber.

clue.text: Mid-West city invaded by Americans one summer

definitions.meaning: a city in Nebraska in the American Midwest
the codename of a Normandy beach stormed by US troops on D-Day, June 1944

explanation.surface: A Midwestern town was overrun by Americans in summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is a Nebraska city and the D-Day landing beach shared its name.

clue.text: Worker in firm producing section of poem

indicators.note: in places the insect inside the company abbreviation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
a worker ant is the standard crossword worker

explanation.surface: An employee of a company writes verse.
explanation.definitionFit: A canto is a major division of a long poem.

clue.text: Animal in a Parisian outhouse, safe and sound

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: in puts the animal inside the other letters

parts.note: a shed is an outhouse
a cat is an animal

explanation.surface: A French cat in a garden shed is perfectly fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscathed means unharmed, coming through without injury.

clue.text: Line of verse about a line in mathematics

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the verse term goes round the single letter

parts.note: a dimeter is a line of verse of two metrical feet

explanation.surface: A poetic line concerning a mathematical line.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is a straight line through the centre of a circle.

clue.text: Gorge from food container over there

parts.note: a can is a tin for food
yon means yonder, over there

explanation.surface: A tin of food left in the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A canyon is a deep narrow valley, a ravine.
